@@40088768 <h> Analysis : At UN , world leaders grapple with fragmented world <p> UNITED NATIONS ( AP ) -- To watch events unfold at the United Nations this week -- the parade of human leaders bringing their entreaties to the rostrum one after another -- was not unlike being a therapist right before the holidays , watching the couch as the appointments go by . <p> There was confusion . Doubt . Hand-wringing and finger-pointing . Lament about persistent problems , and complaints about prickliness and aggression and others ' unwillingness to get along . Over it all , a generally angsty fog hung . <p> Except these particular complaints -- in speech after carefully calibrated speech , delivered in many tongues -- were not of a personal nature . They were the epic problems of the wider world . <p> Terrorism and tribalism , organized crime and cybercrime , poverty and climate change , post-colonialism and corruption and migration and sustainable development and gender bias and genocide -- a we-didn't-start-the-fire catalog of concerns about what 's wrong with the only planet we have . <p> Insight by Lookout : Federal security and IT practitioners examine the state of @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . Secretary-General Antonio Guterres set the tone the moment he opened the General Assembly debate . " Our world , " he said , " is suffering from a bad case of ' Trust Deficit Disorder . ' " A flood of agreement followed , uttered by leaders in many of the planet 's tongues . <p> " Nations are pulling in new directions , stretching the threads which hold us all together , and pushing the world to the edge , " said Hilda Heine , president of the Marshall Islands . <p> They talk nonstop here of working together , of constructing a world where people get along cheerfully and pragmatically . But even in an interconnected era , as their own remarks underscore , it 's never been harder . The technology that has stitched people into global communities also divides them , and old enmities can now be refreshed and amplified globally in an instant . <p> In short , most of us humans are led by women and men struggling to figure out the same fragmented world that vexes the rest of us . Multilateralism @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the U.N . General Assembly makes clear that the world 's most powerful people are engaged in a massive global effort to manage change . <p> " We are seeing divisions not just among global leaders and nations , but within our own societies , neighborhoods , and even families , " said Joseph Muscat , the president of Malta . <p> It 's not that life is necessarily getting worse overall . Much research suggests that the human race is generally better off than it has ever been , and on its way up in lots of ways . That hope was reflected in the leaders ' speeches in many ways , but it was easy to miss that amid all the trepidation . <p> When are the best dates to retire ? <p> A key problem is this : The very goal that so many leaders advocate -- a multitude of diverse and vigorous voices , treated equally no matter their size -- also happens to be the very thing that we are all wrestling with . Indeed , technology and the way it connects people , in @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ theme -- as did the struggle to harness it , if not outright master it . <p> " The world is flooded with information . One becomes indifferent . It all starts to look like a big show , " French President Emmanuel Macron said . " It all starts to look like even the worst things can become ' trendy ' . It becomes difficult to extricate the cause from the effect . " <p> This is , of course , the fundamental and usually unspoken problem with multilateralism . It 's by definition fragmented . Dictatorship may be many bad things , but it can be more coherent and efficient in the short term . That can be an appealing proposition to people hungering for order in the most complex era that humanity has ever endured . <p> At a time when getting along seems like such an impossible endeavor , and when trying to figure out how to negotiate space with thousands of people who are suddenly on your phone and in your virtual face , the notion of going it alone can be alluring . " @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ at first , " Brazilian President Michel Temer said . <p> But full-on multilateralism -- scorned by U.S. President Donald Trump , who advocates an " America first " policy in its place -- holds its own perils of false promise . The United Nations has struggled at times for relevance and a place in the diplomatic ecosystem , and even its biggest proponents worry it sometimes falls short . <p> " Today we wish to think that our multilateral institutions , including these United Nations , are strong enough to take a stand against aggression and disregard of international rules , " Lithuanian President Dalia Grybauskaite said . " Yet sometimes reality tells a different story . We see a world that is more fractured and institutions that are crumbling instead of sheltering us from the use of force and economic storms . " <p> The United Nations , by its very name , was founded on a dream of ordered collaboration and a jointly charted path forward . Some believe deeply in that ; others , suspicious , call it a haven for globalists and a menace to @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ those two choices are often the either and the or . <p> But what if there was another possibility ? <p> What so many leaders seem to be grappling with this week is the very nature of the new world they are helping to shape . These days , that world is more like a Twitter feed than a book . And the skills they grew up with -- approaching the act of governing as a series of coherent chapters -- are falling short . <p> Maybe , this community of nations has entered a plastic moment . Maybe all the fragmentation of the early 21st century has made things flexible and ripe for retooling , remolding , reshaping . <p> Maybe this year 's General Assembly theme , " making the United Nations relevant to all people , " is really about pointing the world 's countries toward managing the splintering of pretty much everything that leaders say their nations are struggling with -- a fragmentation that is so confusing because it colors so far outside of the lines of traditional sovereignty . <p> Speaking to the General Assembly @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ noteworthy . For his nation , he said , the goal of diplomacy is " to make the future of the world and the region something that is certain . " <p> It never will be , of course . But the managing of humanity 's different fragments in a way that strives for coherence and collaboration , filling in some 21st-century mortar between the enduring bricks of traditional governing , might make an uncertain age just a bit more navigable . <p> <p> Ted Anthony , director of digital innovation for The Associated Press , has reported from more than 25 countries and has written about international affairs since 1995. 
@@40088997 <h> California moves to protect auto emissions rules from Trump rollback <p> Sept 28 ( Reuters ) -- California regulators on Friday voted to require that automakers stick with Obama-era federal vehicle emissions standards for cars sold in the state regardless of Trump administration efforts to weaken the standards . <p> The move was the latest in running political clashes between the most populous U.S. state and President Donald Trump 's administration over issues running from climate change to immigration . <p> The California Air Resources Board , the state 's air quality regulator , affirmed a provision in its greenhouse gas vehicle regulation that establishes that only cars meeting current federal standards for model years 2017 through 2025 comply with the state 's standards and can be sold there . <p> The vote took place at the board 's monthly meeting in Sacramento . <p> The Trump administration proposed last month to freeze federal fuel efficiency requirements at 2020 levels through 2026 . In that proposal , the administration said stricter emissions standards make vehicles more expensive and less safe . <p> Californias position is nationally significant because the state is the largest U.S. auto market and boasts @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . <p> Also , a dozen states and the District of Columbia have adopted Californias emissions rules , accounting for more than a third of all U.S. vehicle sales . <p> California has long been allowed under a U.S. Environmental Protection Agency waiver to set its own , stricter vehicle emissions rules to fight heavy smog in Los Angeles and other urban areas . The Trump administration has proposed revoking that authority , something that could cast doubt on the state 's powers to sidestep federal standards . <p> In a statement , CARB Chair Mary Nichols said the state would " continue to work to keep a single national program , " but that the vote ensures that California and 12 other states will not fall victim to the Trump administrations rollback of vehicle standards should its proposal be finalized . <p> Automakers have urged California and the administration to reach agreement , rather than face years of uncertainty . Automakers want looser emissions standards because consumers now favor bigger cars that use more fuel . ( Reporting by Nichola Groom ; Editing by David Gregorio )

@@40095024 <h> Gassy cows are bad for the planet ; could seaweed diet help ? <p> The smelly reality is that cows will always pass gas . But if farmers had more access to seaweed , cow flatulence might just stink a little less for the planet . <p> That 's the thesis of a New England-based aquaculture company which is launching a drive to become the worldwide leader in an emerging effort to thwart climate change by feeding seaweed to cows . <p> The concept of reducing livestock emissions by using seaweed as feed is the subject of ongoing scientific research , and early results are promising . University of California researchers have found that cows that eat seaweed appear to emit less methane , a greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming , when they belch and pass gas . <p> But one of the big challenges to implementing the seaweed solution is getting enough of the stuff to farmers , and the kind of seaweed that has shown results in cows is n't commercially farmed . <p> Insight by Lookout : Federal security and IT practitioners examine the state of mobile cybersecurity in this exclusive executive briefing @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ which is in the midst of research at facilities in Vietnam and Portugal that is part of its push to become the first farm to produce the seaweed at commercial scale . The company calls the effort " Greener Grazing " and it expects to be operating at commercial scale in two years , said Josh Goldman , the company 's chief executive officer . <p> " If you could feed all the cows this seaweed , it would be the equivalent of taking all these cars off the road , " Goldman said . " Greener Grazing 's mission is to cultivate this , and accelerate scaling of this kind of seaweed . " <p> The type of algae in question is a red seaweed called Asparagopsis , and it grows wild in many parts of the world . Creating the seed bank will make it possible for farmers to grow the seaweed elsewhere , he said . <p> The effort has attracted the attention of the World Bank , said its senior aquaculture specialist Randall Brummett . He said scaling up farming of the seaweed in the developing world could make livestock operations more climate friendly and boost the economies of poorer nations . <p> Skeptics remain . @@40095664 <h> Related <p> Independence anniversaries offer important opportunities to reflect on the course of national events . <p> As Nigeria 's 58th independence anniversary being marked today , coincides with the 60th anniversary of Nigeria 's export of its first oil cargo , we offer this article as our contribution to the national reflection on a major public policy issue : Herdsmen-farmers conflict . <p> We refer to the oil export mainly to underline an important fact ; that cattle rearing , from which Nigeria ought to be deriving much domestic and foreign exchange revenue by adopting global best practices , has degenerated into a source of national tension , antagonism , visceral violence and bloodletting . <p> This is a policy failure of an epic scale . Yet it would be wrong to attribute this failure to the current administration . <p> Some 389 incidents of herders-farmers conflict were reported between 1997 and 2017 , most occurring in the North Central geo-political zone . <p> According to the Food and Agricultural Organisation , Nigeria had 20.6 million herds of cattle in 2016 placing 14th among the world cattle breeding nations . <p> Coming to grips with the problem @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ us to examine the various rationalisations that have been adduced . <p> By drawing on the various pronouncements of the government leaders , spokespersons of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria ( MACBAN ) and the perspectives of various public commentators and policy analysts ; an aggregate of seven explanations have emerged . <p> Climate Change : As desert encroachment has intensified in Northern Nigeria due to climate change , herdsmen have engaged in habitual seasonal migratory patterns , moving from the semi-arid northern part of the country , during the dry season , to the middle belt and southern part of country to graze their cattle . <p> Climate-induced scarcity of water and viable grazing fields , inevitably translates to an existential concern . <p> That Herders and Farmers perceive the battle for grazing pasture and farmlands a matter of livelihood and survival is real . <p> Boko Haram infiltration of herdsmen : The notion that the attacks attributed to herdsmen may be traceable to Boko Haram is widely presumed . Acceptably , in highly polarized environments , terrorists seek cover under any guise . <p> Whilst @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Task Force , ( MJTF ) , might have compelled Boko Haram insurgents to seek cover for movement and intelligence gathering by embedding themselves within the ranks of herdsmen , the evidence of operational collusion has not been confirmed . <p> Sinister work of foreign marauders : More by default than by design , the intensification of herdsmen/farmers conflict coincides with the spillover from the Libyan and Sahel crises , with the attending proliferation of small arm and light weapons ( SALW ) . <p> Foreign fighters that drifted from Libya have brought with them assault weapons , which they barter for cash , or present as tools that guarantee them job opportunities as herdsmen . <p> Yet , it can not be discounted that some cattle owners , concerned about rustlers , have also equipped herdsmen with assault weapons . <p> Naturally in their enlightened self-interest they loathe any adverse impact on their cattle investment , including restricting movement of herdsmen . <p> In fact , the international best practices in cattle rearing and production do not include tedious movement of cattle or open-grazing . <p> Promulgation of anti-grazing @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ anti-grazing laws is not helpful to the resolution of the herdsmen-farmers conflict , insisting the promulgation of such laws are the cause rather than the consequences of the herdsmen-farmers conflict . <p> What this explanation fails to explain is why herdsmen-farmers attacks have occurred in states that have not promulgated anti-grazing laws , for example , Delta , Edo , Enugu , Kaduna , Nasarawa and Ondo . <p> Surreptitious effort to Islamize Nigeria : This claim has been made by some analysts . <p> However , the President has strongly disavowed that such a plan exists , insisting in his address to the meeting of Catholic Bishops in Sokoto on 9th September that such rumours are spread by persons with injurious schemes on the nation . <p> Naked attempt at land grab : Land remains a scare resource . <p> A particularly disturbing feature of the herdsmen-farmers conflict is the forceful seizure or occupation of land by herdsmen in various parts of the country . <p> This not only discourages private investment but also damages the protection of property rights which is a key feature of market economy and @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Literature , Wole Soyinka , in his open letter of June , 2018 titled " On Demand : A language of non-capitulation , non-appeasement , " to urge the President to send a strong warning that his administration would not tolerate forceful land seizure anywhere in Nigeria <p> A careful review of these seven major explanations shows that there are some serious issues to tackle . <p> Obvious existing gaps in policymaking and responses persist . <p> Also evidence abound of important policy measures that the Federal Government can take to stem the tide of violence , restore property rights , ensure safety , and drive the dairy and leather industries and cattle economy in general to realise their potentials . <p> But those potentials will not be realised unless and until policymakers are able to transcend the traditional binary parameters used to define national challenges and issues . <p> Otobo is a non-resident senior expert at the Global Governance Institute , Brussels .
